text:
alex: Heads up — seeing p95 east-west latency jump to ~180ms between gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-19 during the noon batching window. Spike started ~11:48 UTC, correlates with our peak batch ramp. @ops-oncall can you take?

ops-oncall: On it. Any packet loss or drops visible? Can you grab nstat/tcpdump?

alex: Quick stats: small packet loss (~0.6%) on ifenslave0 on node19. NVLink peerwise looks fine. RDMA counters show tx_retries increasing. Posting clipped outputs below.

alex: ```
# ibv_devinfo -v (node19)
device: mlx5_0
max_qp: 32768
tx_queue_err: 42
rx_queue_drop: 3

# ethtool -S eno2 | grep drop
rx_dropped: 128
tx_errors: 0
```

sara: I also noticed some ECMP hashing churn on ToR logs at ~11:45 — netbot did a small config rollout then. Could be a steering hiccup. @ken any planned net changes?

ken: I rolled out a TTL/MPLS tweak to tor-17 at 11:44 as a one-off fix for a flow-trace alert. It was gradual but non-zero. I didn't touch MTU.

maria: Can we confirm MTU parity between the two hosts? If one side is 1500 and the rest are 9000 we see fragmentation and RDMA fallback behavior.

alex: Good call. Quick check: `ip link show` on both.

alex: ```
# node12: ip link show eno2
eno2: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP
# node19: ip link show eno2
eno2: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP
```

alex: That's the smoking gun — node19 dropped to 1500 MTU somehow and RDMA is unhappy (falls back to IP, triggers retries + higher latency).

ops-oncall: Oof. I'm going to pin flows to rack-local paths and disable RDMA for the affected GPU pool while we fix MTU. Will apply route pref and short-term ip rule.

ops-oncall: ```
# temporary mitigation commands (rolled to 4 hosts)
ip route replace 10.0.0.0/16 via 10.1.1.1 metric 50
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control=bbr
systemctl stop rdma-device-monitor || true
```

deploybot: route-change applied to gpu-pool-3 hosts: gpu-node-12,gpu-node-19,gpu-node-20,gpu-node-21. :white_check_mark:

ken: Checking ansible history — looks like mtus.yml was inadvertently applied to an older image class when we ran a kernel-tuning run last night. It set MTU=1500 for the "legacy-kernel" group which includes node19. Rolling that playbook back now.

ken: Rolling revert to mtus.yml on node19 -> setting MTU back to 9000 and restarting network agents.

alex: As a mitigation for serving we increased batch window to 60ms to absorb jitter (was 20ms). Config change pushed to runtime: `batch_max_delay_ms: 60` for pool3. That reduced tail amplification while we fixed infra.

ops-oncall: After route pin + MTU revert p95 dropped back to ~18ms for the affected pair. Packet drops subsided. Keeping oncall watch for 2 hours.

maria: Need a follow-up: add detection rule for MTU drift (alert when adjacent GPU hosts mismatch MTU or RDMA rollbacks detected). Also add guardrail to netbot so MTU changes require explicit approval for GPU pool subnets.

alex: Agreed. Please open an incident/P1 doc with timeline and remediation steps. Suggest runbook additions: 1) check MTU parity 2) verify RDMA counters before pushing kernel tuning plays 3) automated rollback if RDMA tx_retries > threshold.

ops-oncall: Will file incident and attach relevant logs. For now: monitoring shows stable 5m p95 under 25ms. Keeping watch. :thumbsup:

sara: And we should add a CI check to our ansible PR job that prevents mtus.yml from targeting any host with "gpu" tag unless explicit var GPU_ALLOW_MTU=true.

alex: Perfect. Thanks everyone for the quick triage.

(incident:inspector-bot) System note: incident created -> INC-2024-1789, assigned to eng-infra.
